design_source.summary: The responsive CargoLink prototype is the immutable design source. It contains customer shipment entry, collection-window selection, booking review and confirmation, the tracking timeline, the dispatcher board with its unassigned queue and run stop ordering, and the manager performance summary. The accompanying handoff inventories all 12 release-one screens and explicitly excludes invoicing, payment, live map, telematics, customs, warehouse, and multi-depot screens.

information_architecture.summary: Public entry points are sign in and the tracking-code lookup, which exposes milestones only and never addresses. Customer navigation contains Book a pickup and My shipments; dispatcher contains Board and Depot setup; manager contains Performance and a read-only board view. Authorization selects the workspace, so the UI never offers a role switch in production. Desktop uses a compact header and local navigation; mobile uses a labelled bottom bar. Page titles and breadcrumbs identify context without hiding primary actions.

user_flows.summary: Booking is shipment details, service level and collection window, review, confirm, then tracking code with a timeline and email. A cut-off that passes mid-form moves the promised date, explains the change inline, and requires re-confirmation. Tracking opens a shipment and reads its milestone timeline with any failure reason. Cancel uses a destructive confirmation and becomes depot contact guidance once collected. Dispatch selects an unassigned shipment, assigns it to a run, reorders stops, and advances status; a full run keeps the selection and refreshes. Manager selects a date range and reads metrics plus an accessible table, including a deliberate empty-period state.

screen_designs.summary: The prototype specifies visual hierarchy, controls, spacing, color, status treatments, the customer booking interaction, the dispatcher run workspace, and manager metrics at desktop and below 720px. Desktop booking uses a 280px summary rail beside fluid form content; the board pairs an unassigned queue with the selected run. Mobile becomes one column with two-column window buttons, a collapsed queue section above the runs, and labelled Move up and Move down controls instead of drag. Staff data tables become labelled row groups on mobile. The handoff defines all additional screens and their required loading, empty, permission, error, confirmation, and success variants.

clickable_prototype.summary: Open the HTML artifact in a browser. Customer controls advance from shipment details to collection windows, review, confirmation, and the milestone timeline. The Customer, Dispatcher, and Manager controls switch between role-specific workspaces; the dispatcher view demonstrates assignment, stop ordering, and status actions, and the manager view demonstrates metrics and tabular activity. Fixed demo data keeps the artifact deterministic. It demonstrates interaction and responsive behavior while the approved architecture remains the source of API truth.

screen_states.summary: Every data region defines skeleton/loading, empty, field validation, 403 permission, network failure with Retry, and success. Required-input actions remain disabled with nearby explanation. An assignment 409 preserves the selected shipment, refreshes the run's stop count, and focuses the refreshed run. Booking success is a page state with a copyable tracking code and a polite live announcement. Cancellation is focus-trapped and restores focus, and a collected shipment shows contact guidance instead of a failed action. Status and reorder updates show Saving during optimism and restore the last server value on failure; unknown statuses use a neutral Needs attention label.

responsive_accessibility.summary: Use one column at 320-719px, tablet at 720-1023px, and constrained desktop from 1024px. Body text is at least 16px and targets at least 44px. DOM/focus order follows visual order; inputs have persistent labels and described errors; dialogs trap and restore focus; status combines text and color and a failed delivery always names its reason. Stop reordering is fully keyboard operable and never drag-only. Meet WCAG 2.1 AA, expose chart values as tables, announce async updates through polite live regions, and remove nonessential motion under prefers-reduced-motion.

design_system.summary: Typography is system/Inter with 16/24 body, 14/20 labels, 20/28 section headings, and 28/36 page titles. Tokens are ink #151B23, surface #FFFFFF, canvas #F2F5F8, primary #1B4F8A, accent #C2620A, danger #B42318, border #C9D3DE; spacing is 4/8/12/16/24/32/48 and radius 6px. Reuse Button, TextField, Select, DatePicker, AddressFields, StopRow, StatusTag, InlineAlert, Dialog, Skeleton, EmptyState, and DataTable with default, hover, focus, disabled, loading, and error states.

api_data_mapping.summary: ServiceLevelSelect reads GET /service-levels; BookingForm and BookingReview post /shipments and drive confirmation from the returned tracking code; ShipmentList reads /shipments/me and ShipmentDetail reads /shipments/:id; TrackingTimeline reads the public /tracking/:trackingCode view; CancelDialog uses the cancel PATCH and renders 409 guidance for a collected shipment. DispatchBoard and RunPanel read /dispatch/board, post stops, and recover from RUN_AT_CAPACITY and ASSIGNMENT_CONFLICT by refreshing the run. StopRow reorder uses the stop PATCH with version, StatusControl uses the dispatcher status PATCH with a required failure reason, BlackoutEditor reloads on 409, and PerformanceSummary calls the manager-only route without retrying a dispatcher 403. All instants render in Africa/Cairo and field errors stay next to their controls.

asset_handoff.summary: The prototype and handoff provide the exact layout hierarchy, token values, reusable component inventory, responsive transformations, status/error copy intent, focus behavior, API mapping, and acceptance states. Implement tokens as CSS variables and share primitives while route components own orchestration. Decorative assets must be hidden from assistive technology and meaningful assets named. Analytics and client logs exclude addresses, contact details, and tracking codes. Only final logo artwork and failed-delivery email wording remain open; the CargoLink text mark and confirmed UI copy are approved fallbacks.

project_feature_coverage.summary: Shipment booking is covered by details entry, service level and collection window, review, confirmation, and cut-off recovery. Dispatch assignment is covered by the unassigned queue, run selection, keyboard stop ordering, and the capacity conflict state. Delivery status tracking is covered by the milestone timeline, failure reason display, status controls, and the reduced public lookup. Delivery performance review is covered by manager date selection, summary metrics, empty behavior, and an accessible table. No visual behavior is supplied for excluded invoicing, payment, live map, customs, warehouse, or multi-depot scope.
